The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs new lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1326 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old stated he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

Recent findings suggest that this is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a latest contract at the club.

He mentioned: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'.

In a recent development, hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

In a recent development, he does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Recent findings suggest that here, they rose to salute a newly introduced talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

Industry observers note that the Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Sources indicate that although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

Industry observers note that there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the latest deal, thought to be for five years, the manager noted: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

Gameweek five in the Champions League sees Manchester City and Napoli square off in the League Phase.

These two teams suffered contrasting results in the previous round of fixtures, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into to their latest encounter.

Man City vs. Napoli will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Tuesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal among those also in action at home to Borussia Dortmund.

This Champions League match will take place at Man City’s home the Etihad Stadium, which now holds a capacity of 61,470 spectators following a recent expansion.

Man City have lost only two of their last 27 home fixtures in the group stage/League Phase of the Champions League (W22 D3), though one of those was earlier this season against holders Paris Saint-Germain (4-2).

Man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

Match highlights of Man City vs. Napoli will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and presently sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Recent findings suggest that goal Bayern Munich. Philippe Coutinho. 2-8.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

Industry observers note that real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool right now have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

Published: 15:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 22 November 2026.

Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.

Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.

It has been revealed that well, if he did, it has taken them headlong into another cul-de-sac. That’s how it felt at Easter Road yesterday when they were trounced 4-0 by Dundee United and left second-bottom of the Premiership table with more than a third of the season completed.

It made rather a mockery of the club’s social media channels, the profile pages of which proudly trumpet their newfound status as ‘Premier Sports Cup finalists’… with an exclamation mark and a golden trophy emoji thrown in for good measure.

Recent findings suggest that self-respecting Hibs fans won’t be fooled by the propaganda. Not after a humiliating afternoon on which their much-vaunted anthem, ’Sunshine on Leith’, was belted out by a gleeful away support at Easter Road.

Long before Zac Sapsford’s first-half double and strikes after the interval by Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall, some supporters were digging out their anti-board banners and using a megaphone to voice their frustration with those upstairs.

Malky Mackay is under growing pressure from supporters in his role as Hibs sporting director.

Zac Sapsford scores the first of Dundee United 's four goals against Hibs at Easter Road.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley claims that he alone was to blame for their 8-0 thrashing by Hearts.

This is how it works at struggling clubs, where fans need someone to blame. First, they target players. Then they single out the manager. When his replacement proves to be no more effective, they have little option but to turn their guns on the board.

In a recent development, not that there’s anything wrong with holding the hierarchy to account if they are the common denominator in a lengthy period of under-achievement. There has been little sign of progress at Easter Road since Bournemouth owner Bill Foley sold his Hibs shares back to the Gordon family last year, having suggested that they didn’t listen to his input. Major questions are also being asked of sporting director Malky Mackay who was asked in 2024 to lead and oversee the entire football operation, including recruitment and the appointment of a head coach.

In a recent development, club legend David Gray had his moments as manager, but in the end, supporters wanted rid. Reedijk may turn out to be the real deal but the early signs are that he is struggling with the squad he has inherited. Too many of them failed to do the basics yesterday.

In a recent development, unlike Hibs, Jim Goodwin’s Dundee United are a strong side with a clear identity. Not for nothing have they gone eight games without defeat, but they scored all too easily as they racked up their biggest-ever victory at Easter Road.

Hibs’ squad appears to be weak, imbalanced and too full of ill-advised signings for Reedijk to make the kind of impact he would like. The holes in it are such that he recently opted to use Scotland defender Grant Hanley as an emergency centre-forward.

Reedijk needs to begin an overhaul of that playing staff in the January window, but how much power will be granted in that process? The Dutch coach has already hinted that he will not be given the final say when it comes to transfers.

The fans are nervous about another rebuild under Mackay and his recruitment staff, whose work in the summer window left a lot to be desired. Jason Kerr was a double-winner with St Johnstone, but he has cut a hapless figure at the back. Midfielder Azeem Abdulai, signed on a three-year contract from Leyton Orient, has made only four appearances, just one from the start. And then there is striker Nathan Lowe, on loan from Stoke City, who is struggling to adapt.

Mackay’s record is under heavy scrutiny. He is to be commended for making a profit of around £6million on striker Kieron Bowie, but why has there been no substantial replacement since the striker’s move to Italy nearly a year ago? Can he really argue that expensive signings such as Thibault Klidje and Ante Suto have been value for money?

A club of Hibs’ size, with those resources, should not be in the relegation zone. Nor should they be struggling so pitifully in their own stadium – they have lost nine of their last ten league games there and haven’t taken three points at home since April.

Recent findings suggest that which tees up nicely Dundee’s visit to Easter Road on Tuesday, not least because the Tayside club suffered a humiliation of their own this weekend. While Hibs were conceding four, Steven Pressley's side were shipping eight in a hammering by Hearts that has surely inflicted significant psychological damage.

To his great credit, Pressley insisted afterwards that he alone was to blame for his team’s wretched performance. That may have been true on the night, but over an extended period, a club’s fortunes tend to be shaped by decisions off the pitch. As Hibs have been finding out.

  • Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two newly introduced studies. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The company also rolled out their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has unveiled plans to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Recent findings suggest that roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

But when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

Amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she remarked: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most important value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

It has been revealed that do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, notes public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

In the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

Sources indicate that vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

Today I’m considering buying a prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) in case of a power cut. Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.
  • The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.
  • The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

It has been revealed that christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

It has been revealed that “I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract presently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be said, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The substantial problem facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

It has been revealed that the Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under newly introduced boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

According to recent reports, it was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

According to recent reports, “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager remarked. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

In a recent development, as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Sources indicate that jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

According to recent reports, even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Recent findings suggest that ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

In a recent development, you can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

According to recent reports, it was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a latest look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

Industry observers note that the 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

In a recent development, when Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline claims. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Industry observers note that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Industry observers note that frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:53.

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil returns to one of his former clubs, with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil returns to the bet365 Stadium with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest a 1-0 home loss to Queens Park Rangers after Zak Sturge was sent off in the 15th minute, have left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

With the Lions having failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will feel they are in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic.

While this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that have kept clean sheets in their last three home games, especially against a Millwall team that have conceded 18 goals on the road and are without the suspended Zak Sturge. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 10:35, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:37.

Francesco Pio Esposito was in sensational form on Sunday, scoring a hat-trick in Inter Milan's 4-4 draw with Atalanta BC in Serie A.

The 21-year-old has now netted seven times and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Inter during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is right now a host of speculation surrounding his future at San Siro.

Manchester United allegedly recently scouted the 6ft 3in striker, with the Red Devils planning to bring in a upcoming forward next year.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with Esposito, who has 18 goals and nine assists in 64 appearances for Inter in all competitions.

As expected, the form of the Italy international against Atalanta drew huge praise from the Italian media.

What did the Italian media say about Esposito performance?

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Tuttosport called the striker "Super Pio" and focused on his contribution to Inter's attacking display, but it was still not enough to secure his side all three points.

Tuttomercatoweb remarked "Esposito like Haaland" during their post-match piece, with the Inter forward being compared to Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are expected to put Man United in the market for a new striker in January, but they might have to wait until the end of the campaign to bring in a significant-name player in that area of the field.

Inter are remarked to value Esposito in the region of £84m, but that could prove to be a bargain if he continues to develop throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Man United may bring in an experienced option, most likely on loan, during the January market, before launching a significant-money move for Esposito next summer, providing that they are able to hold off the threat of Premier League relegation.

The most recent game at San Siro was a 3-1 win for Milan as Jovic, Christian Pulisic and Fikayo Tomori found the back of the net. Given that Frosinone are the surprise package of the season so far, tonight could be a much tougher test.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

It has been revealed that ➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

According to recent reports, ➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

Industry observers note that ➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A.   • Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.
  • Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.

Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.

In a recent development, the writing already appears to be on the wall for the 52-year-old. A question of when, rather than if, he is given his jotters.

By all accounts, he hasn’t lost the dressing room. Which is just as well, because he has well and truly lost the punters, whose collective mood shifted from angry to apathetic over the course of 90-odd thoroughly entertaining minutes at Rugby Park on Saturday.

When that happens, it’s a long way back.

McCann knows this himself. It is not as if he is operating with the blinkers on.

It's a tough watch for Neil McCann as his Kilmarnock team go down 4-2 to Aberdeen.

His assessment of his team’s performances week-to-week tends to be pretty honest, as it was again this weekend.

The problem is, as he put it, that he is coming across ‘like a broken record’.

According to recent reports, his team are hopeless at the back and toothless up top, with some encouraging stuff in between. If the supporters are sick of hearing it, imagine how scunnered McCann must feel saying it. He certainly looks it.

If they continue to defend like this, relegation is a nailed-on certainty.

According to recent reports, they shipped four here — and it could have very easily been a few more — to take their tally to 33 conceded for the season in just 14 games. It’s laughable, there’s no other way to dress it up.

Aberdeen’s Kevin Nisbet scored twice in four first-half minutes, capitalising on a woeful clearance from keeper Nico Mantl to put the Dons ahead, before curling a free-kick straight through the weakest wall you’ve ever seen in your life to double the visitors’ advantage.

New Dons boss Mario Frick can't hide his delight after victory in first game in charge.

The third goal — shortly after Greg Kiltie had given McCann’s men a lifeline — was the worst of the lot. Former Rugby Park skipper Brad Lyons ghosted in behind the completely unaware Michael Schjonning-Larsen to head the ball home after Cathal McCarthy failed to stop Nesta Guinness-Walker’s cross from the left touchline.

Shocking stuff all round, and exactly the type of goal which has killed Killie all season — and will continue to do so until something drastic changes.

Let’s not forget, the recent international break afforded McCann and his staff a fortnight to work on things on the training pitch ahead of what is going to be a gruelling winter schedule.

According to recent reports, while the Killie manager will ultimately be the one to pay the price, his players need to have a right good look at themselves too. There was simply no sign of anyone in that backline taking any sort of responsibility.

Kilmarnock’s next three games are against St Mirren, Hibernian and Motherwell — the three sides currently directly above them in the table.

An absolute minimum of four points from that run is required, otherwise this is going to get rather ugly. In truth, defeat in Paisley this weekend may well be the final nail in McCann’s coffin.

On the other hand, things are finally starting to look up for the Dons.

Latest manager Mario Frick has promised to bring heavy metal football to these shores, and if Saturday is anything to go by, the ex-Liechtenstein international is a man of his word.

McCann's job looks to be on the line after bottom club Killie succumbed to another defeat.

His team were a joy to watch going forward here, particularly in the first half.

It was a million miles away from the kind of turgid football offered up under his predecessor as Dons manager, Stephen Robinson.

Speed, intensity, aggression, quality. The performance was full of it.

You could count the number of times the Dons faffed about with the ball on one hand. Every time there was an opportunity to get forward, they took it.

Ante Palaversa, making his first appearance of the campaign, was at the heart of it.

Recent findings suggest that for whatever reason, Robinson never fancied the Croatian, a stance which perplexed the Pittodrie faithful. Indeed, the 26-year-old — once on the books of Manchester City — was deemed surplus to requirements over the summer.

The Dons will be delighted there were no takers.

He was outstanding here as he commanded that space between midfield and defence without breaking sweat. Nobody in Killie colours could get near him.

Both Nicky Devlin and Guinness-Walker bombed up their respective wings all day, while some of the link-up play between Nisbet — who should have had a hat-trick before Findlay Marshall wrapped things up late on — and Hicham Mahou was delightful.

Defensively, they were all over the shop at times, and no doubt they will be punished heavily at Ibrox on Tuesday night if they are as open as this.

In a recent development, but this was a display to simply be enjoyed rather than picked apart. It makes a change.

KILMARNOCK (4-2-3-1): Mantl 3; McCarthy 4, Kamson-Kamara 3 (Brandon 46), Stanger 4, Schjonning-Larsen 4; Lowery 6, Tshibola 5 (McKenzie 85); Ring 3 (O’Hara 46), Kiltie 6 (Clescenco 83), Hugill 5.5; Owen 4 (John-Jules 54). Booked: Owen, Hugill. Manager: Neil McCann 3.

ABERDEEN (4-1-3-2): Muller 5; Devlin 6, Molloy 6, Milne 6, Guinness- Walker 7; PALAVERSA 8 (Aremu 61); Lyons 7, Briedl 7 (Mouloula 61), Armstrong 6.5 (Marshall 71); Mahou 6 (Smith 80), Nisbet 8. Booked: None. Manager: Mario Frick 7.

Arsenal's showdown with Borussia Dortmund is arguably the pick of the matches, with those teams sitting at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga tables.

As highlighted by Sports Mole, there are just four players serving suspensions ahead of matchday five.

Fresh off the back of a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Manchester United make the trip to Sporting Lisbon without Matheus Cunha.

As for AEK Athens, Aboubakary Koita is unavailable for their match against Como due to the red card that he was given versus Real Madrid.

Koita was handed a red card after the final whistle for a prolonged confrontation with the officials.

Sabah defender Aden McCarthy is the fourth player to miss the MD5 for his dismissal in the 4-1 defeat to Viking FK.

He now misses the home fixture against La Liga champions Barcelona.

Although Koita and McCarthy will miss matches this week, UEFA are at the moment indicating that an extra game may be added to their suspensions in due course.

Chris Sutton has noted he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘new manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor concerns over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

It has been revealed that the Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 12:02.

Sources indicate that paris Saint-Germain have recently made enquiries about Estevao and Rayan, who are not available in the January transfer window. The capital club have a third, more accessible Brazilian talent on their radar.

Recent findings suggest that injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue could force PSG to revise their plans for the January window. Both forwards have suffered anterior cruciate ligament ruptures and could miss the whole season. Faced with these two major absences, boss Luis Enrique and Luis Campos are studying different options to strengthen the Parisian attack.

With Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner ruled out as options, the French club have notably made enquiries about three young Brazilian talents in recent weeks, according to TeamTalk.

PSG contacted Chelsea to find out the conditions of a possible transfer for Estevao. The 19-year-old winger, who arrived from Palmeiras, is highly rated by the Parisian hierarchy. His limited playing time this season had raised hopes of an opening, but Chelsea swiftly ruled out that possibility.

The London club are counting on their Brazil international for the coming years and do not wish to part with him, even temporarily.

The situation is similar for Rayan. The 20-year-old winger, who plays for Bournemouth, is also on the Parisian radar. But Bournemouth are no more inclined to let their gem leave in the middle of the season.

According to the outlet, another Brazilian gem is being closely watched by the Parisian recruiters: Alisson Santana.

Industry observers note that the 21-year-old winger currently plays for Shakhtar Donetsk and is enjoying a convincing start to the season. The Brazilian has scored six goals and provided five assists in 16 games. His performances have attracted the attention of PSG scouts.

It has been revealed that alisson is regarded as 'a much more accessible target' by TeamTalk. Currently valued at £11m (€13m), the recently capped Brazil international would, however, be more of a long-term signing than one for the second half of the season. His profile could also raise questions, as he is mainly used as a right winger, while versatility is very important to Luis Enrique.

Industry observers note that PSG have not, however, limited their search to the Brazilian market. Two other attacking profiles followed in the Bundesliga, Ibrahim Maza and Said El Mala, who has already reacted to the PSG rumour, are also among the players liked by the Parisian recruitment team.

The recruitment team still have six weeks before the January transfer window opens.

“No, there’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United,” he said.

“I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester! Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always highlighted how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always stated, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club states, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.

“Yes, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, reveals that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.

“My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am. I will never hide from that, I will never say, no, our position at the moment needs to be to get top four.”.

In a recent development, recently, Fernandes’ name has been mentioned in conjunction with Milan, who are looking to boost the level of their squad with quality signings. The former Sporting CP man knows head coach Ruben Amorim well, and could help fill the void if Luka Modric retires/departs.

Fabrizio Romano even spoke of the idea being ‘more than a dream’ for the Rossoneri management, while The Athletic also reported that the 32-year-old is an option Milan are exploring after he turned down United’s second offer.

Since joining Manchester United in January 2020, Bruno Fernandes has recorded 113 goals and 111 assists in 340 appearances across all competitions.

#107413. Chelsea news: The nine mistakes Xabi Alonso has made as Blues manager

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Chelsea news: The nine mistakes Xabi Alonso has made as Blues manager

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1132 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.
  • Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.
  • Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.

Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.

Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.

Should Chelsea lose at Nottingham Forest - another team far more physically-imposing than themselves - on Friday night, Alonso's win percentage after 15 matches would be almost identical to that of Liam Rosenior's after 23 games.

While that creates an argument that Chelsea's players are to blame for their fall from grace rather than the Spaniard or Englishman, Alonso is responsible for a number of baffling decisions during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Here, Sports Mole highlights nine mistakes that Alonso has made since he was announced as the club's latest manager in May.

With Valentin Barco announcing that he was leaving Strasbourg on May 19, the deal to take him to fellow BlueCo-owned club Chelsea could have been concluded before Alonso's appointment.

However, for unknown reasons, it was not unveiled until August 2, suggesting that there was time for Alonso to veto the transfer.

It has been revealed that at 5ft 7ins and of slender build, Barco is simply not equipped to be a Premier League midfielder. While he may have starred for Strasbourg, the Argentine is not a suitable fit alongside Chelsea's other engine-room options.

He has reached this stage of the season with three starts and four substitute appearances, with just 25 minutes coming since October 10.

Given the amount of game time that Marco Palestra was given during pre-season, it was clear that Alonso viewed the Italian as a first-choice pick at full-back or wing-back.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, Alonso got carried away. Palestra racked up 311 minutes across four pre-season friendlies played between August 1 and August 15, and the former Atalanta BC player suffered an injury in the days before the opening Premier League game of the season against Fulham.

That prevented the Serie A defender of the year from making his debut until October 10, effectively having to play catch-up as he attempts to acclimatise to English football.

While the 21-year-old started the recent win over Manchester United, he is yet to convince in his current role.

After an extended season that saw him represent Ecuador at the World Cup on July 1, Moises Caicedo was back playing friendlies for Chelsea in the Middle East by August 5.

The midfielder subsequently started three friendlies across 10 days and, like Palestra, suffered an injury in the build-up to the Fulham game.

Caicedo then lasted just 14 minutes on his return from the substitutes' bench against Brighton & Hove Albion six days later and was not seen again until October 10.

He has suffered with a lingering issue ever since, and the way in which Alonso used players during pre-season deserves more scrutiny than it has done.

Alonso went from naming a stronger team than anticipated against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round to making many alterations versus Leeds United in round three.

Some of that decision-making was justified, yet Alonso himself has taken responsibility for making what he notes were too many changes for the latter match.

Chelsea ultimately came from 2-0 down to prevail by a 6-3 scoreline in a crazy game, but withdrawing Estevao Willian after 45 minutes started the ball rolling when it came to the Brazilian's frustration over his game time.

Not only did Jordan Henderson make his first start since the World Cup, with no pre-season, in this match, Alonso partnered the veteran Englishman with Barco, who was making his first Premier League start for Chelsea.

Although Chelsea held Brentford for the first hour and Henderson produced a solid performance on debut, this game exposed that Barco weakens Chelsea's midfield, rather than add any match-winning qualities.

Romeo Lavia also remained an unused substitute in this contest, one which Chelsea lost by a 3-0 scoreline.

While some Chelsea fans had been waiting for Geovany Quenda to be handed his first start for Chelsea, they did not anticipate it coming in a London derby against Tottenham Hotspur.

Furthermore, his selection led to Morgan Rogers taking on the number nine role, rather than Danny Welbeck, in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro.

In a recent development, chelsea subsequently produced one of their most ineffective performances in the final third this season. That was not necessarily because of Quenda, but more through a lack of a traditional number nine to trouble the Spurs defence.

Two weeks later, Alonso chose the same approach against Sunderland, this time using Pedro Neto down the middle.

This decision was essentially made because Chelsea beat Manchester United in the previous game, yet the Red Devils had been the better team in the first half at Stamford Bridge without scoring their opener.

Although there is an argument that Welbeck has not made the expected impact at Chelsea, the 35-year-old has not been given a chance to build up any rhythm and is immediately benched on the back of an ineffective performance.

Despite Emiliano Martinez being signed from Aston Villa to be Chelsea's number one, the Argentine had hardly been at his best prior to suffering a fractured jaw at Everton on October 17.

Meanwhile, Mike Penders recovered from a mistake on his first Premier League start against Spurs to deliver strong showings versus Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, with the only two goals that he conceded coming from penalties.

Regardless, Martinez was back in the starting lineup against Leeds on Saturday, the 34-year-old conceding four goals and making Chelsea appear more vulnerable in defence than they already were.

Alonso has previously indicated that players will be selected on form, but this was a glaring example of choosing status over performances.

Martinez has now conceded 15 goals in 615 minutes for Chelsea. Penders has shipped seven goals in 555 minutes.

Estevao had already struggled against Leeds earlier this season, so the starlet being drafted back into the Chelsea XI for a second Stamford Bridge game versus the Yorkshire giants felt strange.

Furthermore, his inclusion was ahead of Neto, who is Chelsea's strongest winger when it comes to strength and defending. Alonso has already recognised this by using the Portuguese as a wing-back this season.

Neto being omitted from the first XI for a game against opponents of the profile of Leeds made no sense and was more muddled thinking from Alonso. Chelsea were already 3-1 down before he was introduced as a substitute.

Tech Report: AI is turbocharging cyberattacks — can computer scientists catch up?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.
  • The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.
  • At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.

At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.

Although probably unrelated, these incidents highlight a broader transformation in cybersecurity, say researchers. Artificial intelligence is changing how software vulnerabilities are discovered, allowing both attackers and security specialists to examine vast quantities of computer code at unprecedented speed.

“I think vulnerability discovery without AI is basically dead,” says Steven Murdoch, a computer security researcher at University College London. Researchers in the field who don’t use the technology now risk falling behind, he says.

AI can find weaknesses in software much faster than humans can, giving attackers time to exploit vulnerabilities before organizations can fix them. Researchers now want to understand how thoroughly AI can check software for security flaws, and whether it could introduce latest weaknesses.

Agentic systems help attackers identify security vulnerabilities more rapidly and systematically. While hackers previously had to spend hours inspecting websites and probing software for weaknesses that offered unauthorized access to networks, AI agents use automated tools that can search millions of lines of computer code.

Google has reported that attackers have already used agentic AI to examine software updates, identify the security problems they address, and then find ways to exploit them.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

Sources indicate that “For me, it's about the scale,” notes Daniel Gardham, a cybersecurity researcher at the University of Surrey. AI tends to find the same kinds of weaknesses as human hackers, but it makes it easier for people with limited technical expertise to break into systems.

“They can set an AI agent off and come back in 20 minutes and have dozens of results already,” he says.

It has been revealed that even with AI, most security breaches still involve human failure, he says, such as weak passwords (a common problem with Europe’s supermarket freezers was that passwords were defaults such as ‘admin’ or ‘12345’) or clicking on links from unfamiliar sources. AI-crafted messages can make such phishing messages more convincing and so more likely to succeed. They can draw on publicly available information to personalize fraudulent communications and make them appear authentic.

Sources indicate that murdoch says AI is particularly good at discovering familiar kinds of software flaws, even if the most accomplished human researchers remain better at finding entirely new types of weakness. “They don't need to sleep,” he says. “You can happily work a hundred of them in parallel.”.

Sources indicate that these capabilities of AI helped discover security flaws in Java and PHP software, two programming languages that build cross-platform software and websites. In the Java case, for example, AI identified circumstances that could allow an attacker to corrupt computer memory. But Murdoch says the significance of the concern has been exaggerated.

The Java vulnerability, he says: “Is a real problem, but it’s not one of the top ten vulnerabilities this year or probably even this week.”.

Just like hackers, cybersecurity researchers are using AI tools to promptly and efficiently find weaknesses in computer systems. Murdoch says this has become increasingly crucial to vulnerability researchers, who can now examine much larger quantities of software and work out how to patch up the defences where necessary. Researchers are also developing AI agents that can detect and repair vulnerabilities automatically.

When security researchers uncover a weakness, they typically notify the software developer privately, allowing engineers to prepare a remedy before publishing details of the problem.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

Murdoch states the use of AI in cyber security has shortened the time window between public disclosure and attempted exploitation – from several weeks, to just a few days.

Recent findings suggest that rushing an revision can bring its own problems. A software patch can interfere with other programs and cause the sort of outage that organisations are trying to avoid.

“The life for the defenders who are trying to fix things has become significantly harder,” Murdoch says.

Industry observers note that it’s unlikely that the recent tech outages were connected as large-scale cyber-attack, says Murdoch. The most prominent disruptions, he says, are likely technical malfunctions rather than anything more sinister.
