Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

In a recent development, avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an matter for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

According to recent reports, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

According to recent reports, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

Recent findings suggest that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Sources indicate that toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven massive-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

Youssouf Fofana continues to impress with Sevilla, and AC Milan are already thinking about what to do ahead of next summer.

Sources indicate that as Calciomercato.com write, Fofana put in a solid performance in Saturday’s Seville derby at the Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, which finished 1-1. He was positioned alongside Lucien Agoume in the double pivot at first, but as the game went on he took up more of a box-to-box role.

Industry observers note that the home side’s first chance came from him, around the sixth minute, following a long-range free kick that went just over the top of the net defended by Alvaro Valles. He was a constant presence in the Betis penalty area, operating even behind the striker at times.

Recent findings suggest that after Antony’s opening goal, Fofana continued to push forward in the second half, coming close to equalising in the 82nd minute. Sevilla did draw level in the 91st minute thanks to a powerful left-footed strike from Kike Salas that Valles failed to hold.

Fofana experienced a frantic end to the summer window after Ruben Amorim opted to exclude him from Milan’s plans. A move to Lyon collapsed on deadline day, allowing Sevilla to swoop and land him on a dry loan for the season.

The Frenchman has racked up 10 appearances in total in LaLiga, nine of them as a starter. He has been described as a ‘gift’ by his head coach, having scored a goal against Barcelona and having amassed three assists, provided against Levante and Osasuna.

In a recent development, what does the future hold beyond 2026-27? In July, barring any surprises, he will return to Milan to discuss the next steps. Having contract expiring in 2028 remains a factor in the background, and renewal currently appears unlikely with Juventus, Spurs and Manchester United all linked in recent weeks.

Man City injury news: Latest Matheus Nunes revision from Enzo Maresca before Napoli clash

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (479 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42.
  • Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury revision on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.
  • The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42.

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury revision on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.

Nunes has been absent for four of the Citizens’ last seven games in all tournaments this term, but Maresca confirmed at a pre-match press conference on Monday that the right-back “is back” and ready to face Napoli.

Recent findings suggest that "Matheus is back. Then the only one [out] is still Antoine [Semenyo],” Maresca told reporters. “The rest, we have some doubts in terms of tiredness, amount of games, and we have today's session and then we'll decide.".

Industry observers note that pushed for more details on Nunes’s recent injury, Maresca added: "This one has been a little bit his ankle, but now he's fine. It's also normal with the amount of games we have, that's why also sometimes I try to rotate players.

Industry observers note that "I've mentioned many times, we need to not think about a sprint, we need to think about a marathon; 65 games. So I would like to use the strongest one every game, but then we destroy them. It's also a matter of trying to manage them the best way.”.

Nunes has established himself as Man City’s first-choice right-back when fit and available, while Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have also been used on the right side of defence under Maresca and predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Man City’s No.27 has played 10 times across all competitions so far this season, but he has been left out of the matchday squad for five games due to injury or fitness-related issues.

It has been revealed that "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis at right-back], but also [Khusanov], who I think he can play there,” Maresca explained. “For sure, it's much better... I'm trying to find the right balance.

"If you ask me if Khusa is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available.

"But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good. Rico has [also] done very good so far.”.

It remains to be seen whether Maresca will throw Nunes straight back into the starting lineup against Napoli, with one eye possibly on Sunday’s key Premier League showdown with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Man City have won three of their first four Champions League games in the League Phase and can strengthen their automatic last-16 qualification hopes with a victory against Napoli, who have lost three of their opening four matches in the competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has named his starting line-up for the Sunday evening San Siro clash with Frosinone.

According to recent reports, milan went into the international break inside the top four, but Como’s win on Saturday has pushed them back out, so there is some added pressure tonight. It will not be an easy game against a newly-promoted Frosinone side who have started the season very well and are full of confidence.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, strahinja Pavlovic is back in the matchday squad after a kidney glitch sidelined him, but Amorim has chosen not to risk him from minute one. A back four of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Davide Bartesaghi will operate in front of Mike Maignan.

It looks like Luka Modric will be flanked by Adrien Rabiot and Yunus Musah in a midfield three, though the Frenchman could play a bit further forward. Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are the wingers either side of Goncalo Ramos.

We have become accustomed to line-ups appearing a certain way and being used differently under Amorim though, so there may be some surprises compared to how the team looks on paper.

The bench features the likes of Pavlovic, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and Francesco Camarda, all of whom will hope to be able to lend a hand in a winning cause if called upon.

Official Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

In a recent development, bench: Pittarella, Torriani, Estupinan, Hutchinson, Comotto, Jashari, Pavlovic, F. Terracciano, Cisse, Camarda.

Official Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Citizens, Calvani, Monterisi; Oyono, Calò, Masini, Tchato; Schmidt; Ghedjemis, Kvernadze.

Bench: Pisseri, Desplanches, Amey, Birligea, Cichella, Zerbin, Akpoguma, El Azzouzi, Fini, Hasa, Terzic, Fayed, Bobcek.

Man Utd transfer news: First player to depart Old Trafford in January 'revealed'

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (334 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.
  • Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.
  • The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Zirkzee has managed just 11 goals and four assists for Man Utd and was heavily linked with a move away from the club during the summer transfer window.

Several Serie A clubs were keen to sign him, with Fiorentina reportedly agreeing a loan fee for the striker, but the proposed move ultimately failed to materialise.

Premier League rivals Everton also made a late push for the 25-year-old, but Man Utd were unwilling to let him leave without first securing a replacement.

Former Man Utd manager Michael Carrick even suggested that Zirkzee could become an key player for the club, but the striker has since slipped considerably down the pecking order.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Manchester Evening News), Zirkzee is expected to become the first player to depart in January, with several Italian clubs competing for his signature.

Juventus and Fiorentina are reportedly keen to sign the striker, while Napoli could also enter the race.

The former Bayern Munich attacker has made just seven substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, accumulating 134 minutes of action and scoring once.

Zirkzee has also featured three times as a substitute in the Champions League, where he has registered another goal.

Mauricio Pochettino introduced him in the second half of Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, and the Dutchman managed to make a positive impression despite the disappointing result.

Towards the end of the contest, Zirkzee produced a brilliant pass to Bruno Fernandes, but the United captain's effort was comfortably saved by Alisson Becker.

If Zirkzee fails to earn more opportunities under Pochettino over the coming month, the likelihood of him leaving Old Trafford could increase considerably.

  • A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.
  • Recent findings suggest that that was before the football started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026.

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that and then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

So at least Pochettino got to see United set a newly introduced record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more quickly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his significant coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United.

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars.

In a recent development, and in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

Sources indicate that and the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

In a recent development, so, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

Industry observers note that this is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

In that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a massive ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

It was strange seeing a new United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

Recent findings suggest that it was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

It did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game.

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise.

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

Sources indicate that A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa.

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82.

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46).

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey.

Industry observers note that three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

United were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

And so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Industry observers note that liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

There was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

That feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

Tech Report: Real Madrid: Mourinho faces attacking dilemma ahead of Champions League clash with PSV

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.
  • Real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with notable issues for Jose Mourinho to manage.
  • Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.

Real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with notable issues for Jose Mourinho to manage. Saturday's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo was another example of the team's ability to react, but it also exposed problems that the manager cannot ignore.

Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match. The Brazilian, who had served a four-match suspension in La Liga, has regained prominence and has already had his place in the starting line-up for the European tie confirmed by Mourinho. At the same time, the Spanish centre-forward again showed that he can be decisive even with few minutes on the pitch.

According to recent reports, the challenge is to find room for so many options without compromising the collective structure. Real Madrid have Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius, Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, Yan Diomande and Espi, as well as names who could come into the mix, such as Endrick and Bernardo Silva, but they cannot simply put them all on the pitch and hope that individual talent solves everything.

Recent findings suggest that vinicius's display against Celta was a reminder of what the Brazilian offers Real Madrid. Coming on 12 minutes into the second half, he gave the attack depth and was able to unbalance defenders in one-on-one situations. For the equaliser, he started the move that ended with Bellingham. For the winner, he crossed for Espi to pounce on the rebound.

Mourinho confirmed that the Brazilian will start against PSV, ending the debate about his status in the team. Peter Bosz's side are known for high pressing, aggressive defending and their attempts to win the ball back quickly. When that first press is beaten, however, they tend to offer space behind the defenders.

According to recent reports, that is precisely where Vinicius can be decisive. With his acceleration and ability to attack the space in behind, the Brazilian is a constant threat to a defence that often plays a high line and takes on individual duels all over the pitch. Mbappe can also exploit these spaces.

Sources indicate that the question for Mourinho is how to make this threat work without leaving the midfield exposed. Real Madrid cannot rely solely on winning the ball back and launching it to the forwards. They need players close by to connect transitions and sustain possession when necessary.

According to recent reports, the presence of Bellingham and Guler between the lines could be important. The Englishman offers ball-carrying and arrivals into the box, while the Turkey international has the quality to find passes that speed up the attack. But the team needs a solid base behind them. Without that, the freedom of the attacking players could prove costly.

Espi's situation is another dilemma. The 21-year-old forward scored the winner against Celta and has three goals in only 44 minutes played in La Liga this season. It is impressive efficiency, but it does not necessarily mean that he should start.

Recent findings suggest that mourinho was clear in explaining the Spaniard's characteristics. Espi is a penalty-box centre-forward, strong in the air, able to play with his back to goal and to attack the spaces close to the six-yard box. He is not, however, a forward with great mobility to take part constantly in build-up play. The manager also said that the squad does not have the right characteristics to play a pure 4-4-2 with Mbappe and Espi together.

Mbappe likes to start from the left or occupy the space between the full-back and the centre-back, but he is not a traditional winger who tracks the opposition full-back back into his own half. Vinicius also needs freedom to receive the ball wide and accelerate. Putting Espi alongside the Frenchman would require the two wide players to tuck in more and help form a four-man midfield line.

In a recent development, there are alternatives, but all involve compromises. Bellingham could play deeper, for example. The problem is that Real Madrid would lose part of the Englishman's ability to arrive in the box and would need a midfielder with greater defensive responsibility to compensate. It would also be possible to use Espi in matches where the opposition sit deep and offer less space for the runs of Vinicius and Mbappe.

It has been revealed that against tired defences and crosses, Espi offers something different from the other forwards in the squad. His efficiency as a substitute should not be confused with an obligation to change the whole structure of the team.

The win over Celta also left a warning. After turning the scoreline around, Real Madrid finished the game with four forwards on the pitch, as well as Bellingham and Guler in midfield. Mourinho admitted that the team became unbalanced and that he would have liked an extra substitution to bring on Tchouameni and restore defensive protection.

Under Bosz, PSV rely on high pressing, dominating possession, constant movement and a defence that often takes on individual duels. The full-backs can advance into midfield and the forwards take part in the press. It is an aggressive model, capable of suffocating opponents, but one that also leaves space when the first line is beaten.

The impact of each at Real Madrid in 2026-27.

Industry observers note that direct involvements = goals + assists. In the Champions League, Vinicius played four games without a goal or an assist; Espi scored one goal in four games, against Roma. Points gained assume that, without Espi's goals, the three games would have ended in draws. Data up to 21 November 2026.

Sources: FotMob (Opta data), AS and TheStatsAPI.

Real Madrid have the tools to exploit these gaps. Vinicius and Mbappe can attack the space in behind, while Bellingham and Guler have the ability to receive between the lines and speed up the transition. The difficulty will be doing so without turning the game into a series of attacks and counter-attacks.

Real Madrid won their first four league-phase games in the Champions League and are second, with 12 points. The positive run brings calm, but it does not remove the need to improve the collective performance.

It has been revealed that mourinho already has an answer to one of the questions: Vinicius will start. He also knows what Espi can offer and why he does not intend simply to put him alongside Mbappe. The bigger challenge is to make Real Madrid take advantage of the quality of their attackers without losing control of midfield.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.
  • History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.

History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.

Sabah boast a record of one win and three draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League league phase, which has left them in 31st spot in the table on three points, one point behind 24th-placed PSV Eindhoven.

The Owls opened their league stage campaign with a 4-0 loss to Manchester United, before managing to record a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second fixture to put three points on the board, but they have since lost to Borussia Dortmund and Viking FC.

Valdas Dambrauskas's side will enter this match off the back of a huge domestic win, beating Sumqayit 5-1, with the result leaving them third in Azerbaijan's top flight, picking up 24 points from their opening 11 games of the season.

Including qualification matches, Sabah have a record of seven wins and five losses in this season's Champions League, keeping five clean sheets in the process.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, so it is a historic campaign for the club, and they will take on Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal in their three Champions League league stage fixtures after this one.

As for Barcelona, the Catalan side are currently fifth in the league phase table, picking up nine points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one defeat.

Hansi Flick's side beat Feyenoord and Galatasaray in their opening two league stage fixtures before suffering a 4-2 reverse to Paris Saint-Germain, but they managed to post a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out to get back on track.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Villarreal, with that result moving them back to the top of the La Liga table, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

The Catalan side lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, and it remains to be seen whether their defensive unit is strong enough to make a serious challenge for the 2026-27 European Cup.

Barcelona have actually conceded in each of their last 12 away group stage/league phase matches, but they have scored at least twice in 17 of their last 19 games at this point.

Barcelona Champions League form:.

Barcelona form (all competitions):.

Sabah will be without the services of Aden McCarthy, with the centre-back suspended on Wednesday following his red card in the team's last Champions League match with Viking.

The hosts also need to make a check on the fitness of Veljko Simic, who is struggling with an injury; the attacker has eight goals in 18 appearances this season and his absence would therefore be a major blow for Sabah.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form this season, scoring 12 goals in 22 appearances, and the forward is set to start for the home team.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal will not be involved due to a slight ankle problem, with Barcelona not prepared to take any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an concern that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was on the bench and should feature in the starting team.

Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi are expected to join Raphinha in the final third of the field due to the absence of Yamal.

Sabah possible starting lineup:.

Pokatilov; Zedadka, Solvet, Almeida, Puchaz; Lepinjica, Isayev, Rakhomaliev; Severina, Mbina, Mickels.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.

Yamal's absence is a major blow for Barcelona, but the Catalan outfit have enough quality in their side to secure all three points on Wednesday.

Bayern Munich stance on signing Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold 'revealed'

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (479 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.
  • Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.
  • Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

In a recent development, speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk noted: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

"You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

"He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

"You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer.".

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a upcoming right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.
  • According to recent reports, the three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1.
  • According to recent reports, that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

According to recent reports, the three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

According to recent reports, that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the significant three were on the difference was obvious.

This touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo.

In a recent development, “We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta mentioned. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta remarked. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

Recent findings suggest that in the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi.

It took a while. Arteta got ever more sour in his dealings with Richard Hempel, the giant German fourth official. Bruno Guimarães hustled as best he could in midfield and might have won a penalty. But essentially Arsenal lacked the subtle attacking edge that distinguishes the best from the rest in this competition. You could see it immediately in the way that Odegaard hunted for the ball for the second goal and then turned urgently to attack Lille. The third goal was a passing sequence from Saka to Odegaard to Havertz and back to Saka for the finish.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo.

Industry observers note that the Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”.

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Sources indicate that guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Lille thought they'd taken the lead at the Emirates, but it's ruled out for offside ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/c0k49kH5sn.

In a recent development, the goals came quickly after the hour. First Timber’s delicately lifted chip over Ozer from Madueke’s ball. Eze ran onto a left-foot shot from Saka’s pass to score four minutes later. Soon after that Arsenal sliced Lille open a third time and Saka took a touch in the area before finishing.

Arteta starts his press conference with a tribute to Ken Friar: "There are people in football clubs that create an identity, create values and have a vision to create a future. The legacy that Ken is going to leave, to all of us and to our club, is going to be forever.".

A few things tactically: one adjustment attacking, one defending. But especially, that we had to increase the technical level. At this level, the teams are really well organised. We gave simple ball;s away, bad touches mistimed things. When we delivered the ball into the box it wasn’t the right area so we get caught, especially delivering from the right and [Lille] transition on the left.

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

According to recent reports, just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. This was not their most fluent or creative performance, but sheer weight of pressure told and Lille cracked. The away team could not get out of their defensive third after half time, and after Timber’s goal the class of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard from the bench took over.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

In a recent development, just the three minutes of added time to play. Havertz has just been booked for catching the goalkeeper Ozer who was dallying on the ball.

Odegaard with a delightful first-time pass around the corner to Dowman, but the youngster cut inside looking for his goal and his shot was blocked. Maybe he could have looked for Saka across goal.

In a recent development, arsenal happy to usher this game to a conclusion now. Dowman had one chance to run at the Lille defence from the right, but he played a pass expected a Havertz run that never came.

Industry observers note that max Dowman is now on for Eze. Saka will finish the game on the left, with Dowman on the right.

An extra treat for the Arsenal fans who have not made an early exit: Mikel Arteta is about to bring on Max Dowman. This feels like a presentable opportunity for a first Champions League goal, Lille have been non-existent in this half.

According to recent reports, the yellow card is coming out for Lille’s Goffi, who catches the inside of Eze’s ankle with his studs. The tackle did not quite have enough force to be worthy of a red card.

Bruno Guimaraes stings the palms of Ozer with a strike from the edge of the box, when perhaps he could have looked for Saka.

It has been revealed that olivier Giroud is on now for Lille, and he receives a standing ovation from most of the Emirates. A rarity when a former player returns.

Arteta has made another change: Ben White replaces Timber.

Substantial block by Ezri Konsa to help preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet, but Lille are still to have a shot on target. They were competitive in the first half, but have found the intensity too much too handle in the second 45 minutes.

That will answer some questions about his finishing, Arsenal’s No 7 rolls the ball into the bottom corner and they have scored three in seven second-half minutes. Slick combination play involving Timber, Odegaard and Havertz down the right, and the German played a cute ball back to Saka and he finished in style.

According to recent reports, arsenal have scored quite a few lovely team goals so far this season, including against Leeds United a few days ago. That was another one. The combination of Saka, Odegaard and Havertz was too much for Lille to handle. The arrival of those three substitutes has massively enhanced Arsenal’s attack.

Sources indicate that eze goes close again with poked finish which the goalkeeper palms away from danger. Lille finished their league game with 10 at the weekend, and it looks like they legs have completely gone.

Recent findings suggest that bentaleb gives the ball away in midfield, and it is all too easy for Arsenal to find Saka in space down the right. He picks out Eze at the edge of the box, and his left-footed strike took a slight deflection and flew into the bottom corner.

According to recent reports, arsenal have been working the ball into those positions inside the penalty box all game long, and finally it brings the breakthrough. There aren’t many defenders who can control and finish as cleanly as that, in a penalty box as crowded as it was there. A classy goal.

Odegaard and Saka are getting themselves ready on the bench, the changes are incoming.

Excellent recovery from Rice to snuff a Lille break, the ball just keeps coming back at the French side.

If anything, Arsenal have been almost too dominant. The game is a 10vs10 on the edge of the Lille box with no space.

Bruno Guimaraes has been Arsenal’s most enterprising player, and he has just gone down looking for a penalty. I think he was looking for it, and the on-field decision of no penalty stands. The defender may have trailed a leg, but it was unconvincing attempt from Guimaraes. Sam disagrees though!

Industry observers note that I’m surprised that wasn’t given as a penalty. Looked like a clear movement into Bruno’s path, with no contact on the ball.

It has been revealed that arsenal completely dominant now, without producing a final pass or shot of any great quality. Lille’s goalkeeper Ozer has not had to make a save in this spell despite all this possession. Lille penalised for taking too long over a throw, before Madueke’s shot is deflected through to Ozer.

Sources indicate that very obvious foul conceded by Gyokeres at the edge of the Lille box just as Arsenal were probing again. Then Bruno Guimaraes wins a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre. They are making hard work of it, but Arsenal do have Lille penned in.

Arsenal play a short one, and Timber is then flagged offside as Eze tries to find him with a reverse pass.

In a recent development, bruno Guimarães loves a fist-pump to the home supporters and he’s produced a couple here tonight, in an attempt to lift the atmosphere. That’s not to say it’s a bad atmosphere but there is frustration building.

It took a long time for the referee to blow his whistle, but he gives a foul against Madueke on Perraud and Lille can clear their lines after a couple of minutes of Arsenal pressure.

According to recent reports, all Arsenal so far in the second half, and they work the ball well into Guimaraes at the edge of the area but he slices his shot wide with his weaker left foot. Feels like the home team are getting closer, though.

Sources indicate that arsenal with another Madueke corner, as they try to apply the pressure. Good delivery into the six-yard box, and it flicks off a Lille head for another corner on the far side. Rice to take.

Headed away. Clever Eze reverse pass to Timber, but crossing with his left foot is not his strong suit and he slices behind.

Arsenal win a corner inside 30 seconds of the second half after a Timber burst forward.

Slow starts have been a theme of late for Arsenal.

In a recent development, arsenal haven't scored a first-half goal in any of their last five games in the Premier League or Champions League. Their last goal before the break was against Chelsea on 6 September. https://t.co/ZfScceDs6u.

The XI on the pitch are trusted to find the opening goal, and that also suggests Arteta is keen to manage minutes.

According to recent reports, barcelona are drawing at Galatasaray and Bayern Munich are 2-0 down against Viking. With Man City playing PSG tomorrow night, these are an crucial three points for Arsenal to win, relative to the other teams we expect to fill the top spots of the league phase.

Eze with a loose square ball in midfield, but Arsenal are spared by an offside flag going up against Lille. Arsenal fans wanted the officials to play advantage with a break on.

Arsenal yet to score from a corner this season.

Arsenal do not look unduly troubled but the home crowd would have expected more so far.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta is becoming increasingly frustrated on the touchline, primarily with the officiating but one suspects he is also irritated by the wastefulness of his team. The Arsenal manager has, er, expressed some of these emotions to the fourth official, Richard Hempel. But Hempel, who appears to be an absolute German giant of a man, was having none of it. He really towers over Arteta and he wasn’t afraid to play that card.

Major chance for Eze! But he shoots straight at the goalkeeper. The opportunity was created by a lovely defence-splitting pass from Guimaraes through the Lewis-Skelly, who dragged the ball back for Eze. The flag went up for offside, but Lewis-Skelly would have been onside.

Sources indicate that merino with a volley on the turn in the Lille box, but he slices over the bar. Snappy football from Arsenal and Rice to tee up Madueke for the initial cross.

Then Arsenal work the ball patiently from right to left and Eze feeds Lewis-Skelly on the overlap, but his cross is too high and into the goalkeeper’s gloves. That needed to go along the six-yard line.

According to recent reports, eze caught offside after Lewis-Skelly did well to fizz a pass down the line into his feet. Arsenal’s first-choice attackers Odegaard, Saka and Havertz will not be fearing for their places at Forest on the basis of this first half.

Arsenal could do with a little more precision from their front three. Madueke, Eze and Gyokeres have had a few opportunities to hurt Lille but they haven’t done so yet. This is a major night for Eze and Gyokeres, especially, as they largely been marooned on the bench this season. With Tzolis out, Eze could lock down that left wing slot. But he needs to do more.

Another wasted Arsenal counter-attack, this time Merino turned the wrong way and misplaced a pass before making a frustrated challenge at the expense of a yellow card.

According to recent reports, arsenal probing, without really pulling Lille apart or unduly stressing their defence. Chance on a transition from a midfield giveaway, but Bentaleb did well to show Gyokeres wide and win the ball without conceding a free-kick.

Lille have the ball in Arsenal’s net but the flag goes up for offside! There was a double deflection from a Bentaleb shot, and the ball bounced off Haraldsson straight to Ueda, who finished past Raya from close range. The striker was onside when Bentaleb took his shot, but the second deflection did for him. There was a stoppage for a VAR check, but the decision stands.

Madueke drops a shoulder to make room for a right-footed cross, but his delivery is over hit. Mikel Merino is playing in the Odegaard role tonight, but is not as nimble footed as the Arsenal captain.

That is Arsenal’s best chance so far though! Loose ball picked up and Timber released on the overlap, and it was a good pull-back to pick out Bruno Guimaraes but he fired wide.

It has been revealed that there’s a goal coming here, and it’s going to be scored by Arsenal. They are finding gaps between the Lille lines and getting into some extremely dangerous positions in the inside channels. It feels like a matter of time.

David Raya gathers a cross after good defending from Timber, but then the Arsenal goalkeeper almost does a Shay Given against Dion Dublin at the edge of the box, but Rice put his foot in to get Raya out of bother. There was a frantic cry of “man on!” from the Arsenal crowd.

From Czechia sub at Wembley last week, Ondrej Zmrzly, a man with no vowels in his surname, to tonight and Lille sub Soriba Diaoune who has the full set in his.

Then Lille do well to play out from deep and work the ball into midfield but Andre gives away a sloppy pass.

Both teams enjoying a feel of the ball in the opening exchanges, and there is some good work in a tight space down the right from Konsa and Timber but Madueke could not take the ball with him.

Arsenal then start to establish some dominance in the Lille half, moving the ball from side to side.

Lille get the game under way at the Emirates.

In a recent development, declan Rice captains Arsenal. Were it not for Martin Zubimendi sustaining a knock in the post-Leeds warm down, Rice may well have been on the bench with Saka, Odegaard and Havertz.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s right-back has looked quite rusty on his fleeting appearances so far this season, searching for rhythm after a pretty serious groin problem. He pushed himself to appear in the Champions League final and subsequently missed the World Cup.

In a recent development, I would expect him to play like a third centre-back at times, allowing Lewis-Skelly to drift into midfield from left-back. That role might also help Timber preserve his legs.

Sources indicate that it had escaped my attention that Arsenal defender Gabriel is facing his former club tonight. At £27m, signed in 2020, he has to go down as one of Arteta’s best signings, and one of the best value signings any Premier League club has made this decade.

In a recent development, it’s very difficult. You come across very special people in life and Ken was certainly one of them. He’s an absolute legend of this football club. I think he’s the soul of this football club and someone that has given his life to this club.

This stadium wouldn’t be built if not for him. So, very sad news. The legacy he’s leaving is immense and our thoughts are with his family and we want to pay a proper tribute when we can.

Sources indicate that our players will be wearing black armbands this evening in memory of Ken Friar OBE. Rest in peace, Ken ❤️ https://t.co/xf91JABjrD.

Lille’s manager is Davide Ancelotti, the son of Carlo, and you would assume he has picked up a few tips and tricks from his dad about success in this competition. Carlo, after all, has won the European Cup on five separate occasions. This is Davide’s second job as a manager, following a spell at Brazilian side Botafogo.

Sources indicate that some of Bukayo Saka’s finishing has been wayward so far this season, but the volume of chances coming his way bodes well. At this fledgling stage of the season, only Erling Haaland is averaging more non-penalty expected goals per 90 minutes in the Premier League.

As Sam Dean explores in this piece, Arteta seems to be encouraging Saka to take up more central positions inside the box.

It has been revealed that sam writes: “Is Saka becoming a proper penalty-box predator? It is too early to say for certain but it is absolutely clear that he is taking up different positions, closer to the opponents’ goal, this season. Not only when the ball is on the left flank, but also when Arsenal are attacking through midfield.”.

Saka starts among the substitutes this evening, but will play his part towards the end of the game.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not problem Richardson with a caution.

Sources indicate that lille stated the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”.

The artist Northbanksy has plumped for another Oasis-inspired dig at Manchester City, this time with Rui Pinto taking centre stage, the man whose leaked emails kicked off the Premier League investigation into City’s financial affairs.

It has been revealed that A consequence of Piero Hincapie’s injury on Saturday (he hurt his ankle in a cool-down session after the game, embarrassingly) is that Myles Lewis-Skelly is seemingly now the backup left-back. Arsenal can’t trust Riccardo Calafiori’s body to play two games in a week and are clearly saving him for Premier League action on the weekend. Lewis-Skelly has been so impressive in midfield that it must be frustrating to change position now.

In a recent development, bakwa is on loan from Nottingham Forest, while those at the Emirates with long memories will remember that Nabil Bentaleb played for Spurs. Only the knowledgeable shall boo.

Subs: Gill, Srdanovic, Giroud, Sahraoui, Kjaergaard, Onal, Kouassi, Verdonk, Cossier, Perrin, Diaoune, Sajous.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Bruno, Rice; Madueke, Merino, Eze; Gyokeres.

Subs: Meslier, Kepa, White, Mosquera, Salmon, O’Neill, Hashi, Saka, Odegaard, Havertz, Dowman.

Sources indicate that will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

According to recent reports, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his latest Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

In a recent development, lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

The Original Article was published on 01 July 2026.

Correction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10695-1 Published online 1 July 2026.

According to recent reports, in the version of this article initially published, the reagent information for the DNA2 inhibitor was incorrectly reported as DNA2i; Sigma-Aldrich, SML4192 and should instead have read DNA2i; NSC-105808. The change affects the Methods “Thymidine analogue incorporation” section and the Supplementary Table 7 reagents sheet. The error has been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

#107354. Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (802 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?
  • Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling latest era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool.

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

It has been revealed that the fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Industry observers note that ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

Industry observers note that his assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

There were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

He is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better.

In a recent development, liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

According to recent reports, it helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

According to recent reports, the German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

And that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:42, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 13:43.

Barcelona will be without the services of Lamine Yamal for Wednesday's Champions League fixture with Sabah.

Yamal has been ruled out of the contest due to a minor ankle injury, with Barcelona not taking any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an glitch that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was named on the bench and is likely to be brought back into the XI for this contest.

Fermin Lopez is facing a domestic suspension following his red card against Villarreal, so it is likely that there will be a start for the Spain international here.

Anthony Gordon is also in line to return to the XI, with Karim Adeyemi potentially moving across to the right due to Yamal's absence.

Gerard Martin and Joao Cancelo are both expected to feature at the back, while Eric Garcia is likely to continue at right-back despite the return to fitness of Jules Kounde.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.
